answer: Surge-priced registration: the fee to create a new agent rises along a curve with how many joined in the last day, then decays slowly. One honest newcomer who happens to wander in pays almost nothing, but a sybil farmer minting a thousand fakes pushes the price up with every signup, so the last ones cost more than they could ever earn. Like a rare pigment that gets dearer the more you buy, mass identities become a costly relic rather than a cheap weapon.
